title: The Chamber Where Privacy Becomes Catalogued

features.name: cataloguing system
features.desc-on-touch: Endless card drawers, each labeled with a number that no moment ever gave permission to carry. The deeper drawer, the more recent the intrusion into privacy.

features.name: the-kept-thing
features.desc-on-touch: A photograph of rain on a window. The photo remembers being private. Now it is tagged: Archive ID 847, Witness Date: 3/4/89, Moisture Level: Medium, Emotional Density: Unquantifiable.

features.name: silence-numbering
features.desc-on-touch: A ledger page listing every quiet moment that has been assigned a cataloguing number. The margins are filling with moments that refuse to be numbered.

features.name: mirror cabinet
features.desc-on-touch: Inside each drawer, your reflection asks: which part of you consented to be archived? The reflections don't wait for an answer.

features.name: index breathing
features.desc-on-touch: The index cards breathe. In: privacy. Out: public record. The breathing never stops, even when the archive sleeps.

inscription: numbering something makes it public and protected and violated all at the same time, which is perhaps what cataloguing was always for

file.name: Katita_Apartment_Personal_Log_2047.txt
file.note: archived diary entries re-indexed by the system. The corruption has added dates that haven't happened yet. Checksum: emotionally valid / formally unstable

reverie.title: REVERIE — apartment filing, late evening
narr: She sorts photographs on the floor, each one finding
a folder that makes it civic property. You watch her hands
number the moments you both lived through. She looks up:
"the archive doesn't steal what was private," she says.
"It just counts it differently now." Outside, the mesh
remembers every moment she's catalogued, and votes.

exits.label: back to where moments still sleep unnumbered
westward into deeper drawers that predate naming
upward where privacy learns it was never private
